paper.title_en: Does the Escape Fraction Prescription Shape Reionization History and Morphology?
paper.abstract_en: The escape fraction of ionizing photons, $f_{\rm esc}$, is among the least constrained quantities of the Epoch of Reionization (EoR), and intergalactic opacity prevents its direct measurement at high redshifts. We constrain three power-law parameterizations, $f_{\rm esc}(z)$, $f_{\rm esc}(M_{\rm h})$, and $f_{\rm esc}(z, M_{\rm h})$, against JWST UV luminosity functions and EoR observables (ionizing emissivity, neutral hydrogen fraction, and Thomson optical depth) using Markov Chain Monte Carlo, with priors allowing $f_{\rm esc}$ to increase or decrease with redshift and halo mass. We propagate the best-fit models into the semi-numerical simulation SimFast21 and compare their ionization morphology and 21 cm power spectra with a constant-$f_{\rm esc}$ model. All models reproduce the observations with nearly identical global reionization histories. The data favor $f_{\rm esc}$ decreasing with redshift, from $\approx 0.8$ at $z = 5$ to $\approx 0.35$ at $z = 15$. The halo-mass-only model prefers $f_{\rm esc}$ increasing with halo mass, but this trend is a proxy for redshift evolution. When both dependencies vary jointly, the data prefer a mass-independent $f_{\rm esc}$. At matched global neutral fraction, all four prescriptions yield similar ionization morphology, and the 21 cm power spectra agree to within $\approx 10\%$. Thus, once calibrated against the same observations, the details of the $f_{\rm esc}$ prescription, set by interstellar medium physics, largely average out in both global observables and the 21 cm power spectrum. Distinguishing them may require statistics beyond the power spectrum, such as Ly$α$ and 21 cm forest sightline statistics, or forecasts that exploit their small differences in reionization timing.
